candidate.answerReason: In the convex quadrilateral, angles A and D are same-side interior angles for AB and CD with transversal AD. Their supplementary sum guarantees AB ∥ CD, so A must hold.

methods.label: Identify the transversal
methods.explanation: Angles \(\angle A\) and \(\angle D\) are same-side interior angles formed when lines \(AB\) and \(DC\) are cut by \(AD\). They are supplementary, so \(AB\parallel CD\). We cannot conclude that \(AD\parallel BC\).
methods.levelReason: Requires only identifying same-side interior angles and applying the Grade 7 parallel-line criterion.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is determining which opposite sides must be parallel from the given angle sum. review.mathematicalCheck: Convexity places B and C on the same side of AD, so angles A and D form the stated same-side interior pair. Their supplementary sum forces \(AB\parallel CD\), selecting A.
